target_customer: App developers and device makers running AI models locally on phones, wearables and small devices
problem: Running AI models on low power devices is hard because of memory, latency and power limits, and cloud inference adds cost and privacy concerns.
business_model: Open source or source-available inference engine and small models with cloud fallback; commercial terms not found
product_category: On-device AI inference engine and tiny models

founders.name: Roman Shemet
founders.background_notes: YC page: former quant and economist with product and data engineering experience.

founders.name: Henry Ndubuaku
founders.background_notes: Author of a Maths, CS and AI compendium per YC page. The founders met through YC co-founder matching in London.

competitors.name: llama.cpp
competitors.what: Open source local LLM inference engine, common mobile starting point
competitors.traction_then: widely used per a benchmarking paper

competitors.name: MLC LLM
competitors.traction_then: widely used per a benchmarking paper

technical_complexity.rationale: Cross platform mobile inference with quantization down to 2-bit and custom tiny models is deep systems and ML work.

defensibility.rationale: Optimization know-how and community adoption, but well resourced alternatives such as llama.cpp and ExecuTorch exist.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: No incumbent action against Cactus found; platform vendors keep shipping their own on-device runtimes.

market_need_then: Interest in local inference was growing; company reports 20.9k GitHub stars and 305k monthly Hugging Face downloads (self reported, 2026), and 500,000+ weekly inference tasks per a directory.

branding.domain_note: Uses cactuscompute.com, with Compute added; another YC company is named Cactus.
branding.brand_signature: Needle and Whistle tiny models with sub-20 MB sizes
branding.community_and_virality: Hackathon with Nothing and Hugging Face in Dec 2025 and press from InfoQ and others.

brand_strength.rationale: Developer attention via open source and model releases, but the name is shared with another YC company and the license is described inconsistently.

outcome_analysis: Cactus Compute is an active Summer 2025 company with open source traction in on-device inference and a growing set of tiny models. Funding is not verifiable from the sources found, so its fundraising progress is unknown. Competition from llama.cpp, ExecuTorch and platform vendors is the main risk.
notes: EveryDev lists a $500K YC deal (Aug 2025) and total $1M, and another listing mentions Oxford Seed Fund and Google for Startups; these are single aggregator sources and unverified. A $7M seed that surfaced belongs to the unrelated Cactus (oncactus). Founder education and employers not found on an opened source.
